land.text: the northern Igbo heartland, under the Southern Nigeria Protectorate in 1911

successors.note: 'until the establishment of Colonial Nigeria in 1911' (lead); the page gives no name for the protectorate.

capitals.name: Nri (Awka area)
capitals.note: The Nri Kingdom page names no capital and gives no coordinates; the dot sits at Awka (gazetteer place), the centre of the northern Igbo core.

correction.text: the nuclear northern Igbo region: 'royal burials have been unearthed dating to at least the 9th century'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The infobox span reads '9th century-1912'; the page gives no founding year (Chambers puts the first eze Nri 'at around 1225 CE'; Angulu's 1043 is flagged self-contradictory) and no area. A 40 km circle round Awka stands for the nuclear Nri country.

correction.text: Nri influence 'extended well beyond the nuclear northern Igbo region' by the late 16th century

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Ritual and trading influence, not a frontier; the Igboland region (about 33,000 km2 in the gazetteer) is a stand-in for the wider sphere, with the Nri-Igbo page naming Awka, Onitsha, Nsukka and Asaba. Confidence 1.

correction.text: 'Nri influence declined after the start of the 18th century'; the kingdom 'survived in weakened form until 1911'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: back to the nuclear region after the decline; the page gives no extent.

region.text: the nuclear northern Igbo region round Awka

ledger.note: 9th century: the Nri kingdom's royal burials. The infobox span '9th century-1912'; 'royal burials have been unearthed dating to at least the 9th century'. The page gives no founding year; Nri-Igbo page: 'The Nri clan existed from as far back as the 9th century.'

region.text: the Igbo country beyond the nuclear region

ledger.note: late 16th century: Nri influence spreads. 'By the late 16th century, Nri influence extended well beyond the nuclear northern Igbo region.' The land is the researcher's reading; ritual influence, not conquest.

region.text: the outer Igbo country, no longer under Nri influence (page silent)

ledger.note: 18th century: Nri influence declines. 'Nri influence declined after the start of the 18th century' and the kingdom 'appears to have passed its peak in the 18th century'. The page names neither the land lost nor who took it.

1911: the British end Nri as a political power. 'A British colonial expedition forced the reigning eze Nri to give up the ritual power of the ìkénga'; remnants of the eze hierarchy lasted 'until the establishment of Colonial Nigeria in 1911'. The infobox says 1912.

region.text: the Nri country, to the British protectorate

ledger.note: 1911: the Nri Kingdom ends as a political power. In 1911, 19 eze Nri names were recorded; long interregnums make exact dates hard.

wars.name: British expedition against the Nri
wars.outcome: A British colonial expedition forced the reigning eze Nri to give up the ikenga, ending Nri as a political power (1911); the infobox end is 1912.
wars.note: The page names no commander, battle or land.

certainty.note: Nri was a ritual kingdom of towns and titles, not a bordered state; no page gives a frontier.

sources.title: Nri Kingdom
sources.note: Infobox span 9th century-1912; royal burials from the 9th century; first eze Nri about 1225; influence beyond the nuclear region by the late 16th century; decline after 1700; 1911 British expedition; no capital, no area.

sources.title: Nri-Igbo
sources.note: Thin: the Nri clan from the 9th century; Awka, Onitsha, Nsukka, Asaba; no founding year, capital, end or Aro.

notes: Nri has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened, both thin on dates and silent on land: every year and shape here is a confidence-1 reading, and the 'extent' is a stand-in for ritual and trading influence rather than a border. The Nri Kingdom page gives two end dates (infobox 1912, text 1911) and two founding claims (Eri in 1043 per Angulu, flagged self-contradictory; 'around the 1500s' per others; first eze Nri about 1225 per Chambers). Not placed: Onitsha (a monarchy using the title Obi), Agbor, Igala, Aro (the Aro dossier is written separately; the Nri pages do not mention it). The capital dot is the Awka gazetteer point, not Agukwu Nri. Counterpart: niger-coast-protectorate stands for the Southern Nigeria Protectorate of 1911 (see that dossier).
